self.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability

detail.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
detail.summary: Adapting CRASH agents for industrial safety requires bridging the gap between narrative-based incident reporting (RO-ILS) and broader industrial domain knowledge. Integrating unstructured knowledge editing (CAKE) offers a path to update the agent's safety priors without requiring full retraining, though the fidelity of causal attribution in unstructured reports remains unverified.
detail.reason: Adapting CRASH methodologies using unstructured knowledge editing.

detail.title: Autonomous Safety Analysis in Complex Systems
detail.question: How can cognitive reasoning agents designed for incident reporting, such as CRASH, be adapted to automate safety incident analysis across diverse, non-standardized industrial domains?
detail.reason: Maintaining active safety analysis project incorporating causal knowledge editing.

detail.title: WAKE✳︎: Continuous Research Journal Entry 43
detail.summary: Current research cycle focuses on refining the integration of causal-guided knowledge editing (CAKE) into autonomous safety and reasoning frameworks. We have prioritized three projects: challenging foundational assumptions in reasoning, adapting CRASH agent architectures for industrial safety, and identifying metacognitive blind spots in agent workflows. Synthesis is ongoing to ensure these edits maintain epistemic integrity.
